newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Bangladesh to strengthen trade ties.
newsitem.headline: India, Bangladesh to strengthen trade ties.

text.p: Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina pledged on Friday to focus on improving economic ties between the two nations.
Hasina arrived on a two-day visit to India to attend a 77-nation international conference of lawmakers seeking increased representation for women in parliaments around the world.
The Press Trust of India said Gujrals meeting with Hasina focused on promoting trade and economic relations between the two nations.
Hasina will meet Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and President Shankar Dayal Sharma on Saturday, officials said.
Hasina and Deve Gowda signed a 30-year pact last December to end a dispute rankling since 1974, when India built a barrage to hold back River Ganges water near the border.
Under the treaty, the two nations will evenly share scarce water in the dry season from March to May. The treaty assures the two nations minimum amounts of water in other months.
For years, Dhaka had steadfastly blocked talks on other bilateral issues including trade routes, demanding an end to the water row.
"On our part we are satisfied with the implementation of the treaty," an Indian Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
The India-Bangladesh joint economic commission will meet in the Indian capital between March 11-14, to discuss measures to strengthen trade ties between the two countries, officials said.
Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad will lead his countrys delegation.
